text:
marta: FYI CI for sample-app onboarding is failing after the latest typegen regen.

marta: Root cause looks like a semver bump in package.json plus nondeterministic property ordering in the generated OpenAPI client. tests: failing snapshot + publish blocked on the samplekit pipeline :facepalm:

ci-bot: [circleci] build 2345 failed on step "publish-sampleapp" — exit code 1. full logs: https://circleci.example/2345

sam: ugh. which commit caused it? PR?

marta: it's from PR #4521 (auto-typegen). The regen diff shows `package.json` went from 1.2.3 -> 1.2.4 and a bunch of param order changes in `types.ts`.

ricardo: Could be the openapi generator sorting change. We merged the new generator version last week.

jen: Is the semver bump intentional? CI should only bump patch when API surface changes, otherwise we keep patch stable.

marta: I didn't expect the bump. The typegen script now reads `version` from spec.metadata and writes it into package.json. For this spec the `info.version` changed by a build-time timestamp (bad). 

sam: OK quick mitigation — revert the version write in typegen and re-run regen, then we can re-run CI

ricardo: Also we should pin the codegen that introduced the nondeterministic ordering. I saw a change in `sortProperties: true -> undefined` in generator config.

marta: Repro locally with:
```
git checkout origin/pr/4521
yarn && yarn regen
git diff --staged
```

jen: If we revert in PR, we need a hotfix PR to fix the generator config and an additional PR to normalize spec.info.version to a semver-like constant.

sam: I'll open the revert PR and include a changelog note. Also adding a regen CI guard: if regen produces diffs we fail fast with an explanatory message.

marta: Good. For the long term: add a deterministic sort step in the OpenAPI -> typegen pipeline and a test that runs `yarn regen` in CI and ensures no diff on master.

ci-bot: [bot] created issue #789: "deterministic-typegen-and-regendiff-guard" assigned to @sam.

ricardo: One more: sample app publishing should not be blocked by a patch bump in the generated client. We need the publish flow to treat generated-package patch bumps as no-op for release gating unless tests truly fail.

jen: We can change publish gate to check only human-authored package.json diffs (heuristic: files under `src/` vs `generated/`).

sam: I'll put together the revert + regen CI guard PRs, aim to have in by EOD. cc @marta @jen

marta: Thanks. If anyone hits the same locally DM me, I have a small script that normalizes info.version to `1.2.3` before regen.

sam: :thumbsup:
